case1.title: The Stalled Shipment
case1.intro: Three days ago you ordered headphones from Zahw Store. Today a message about the shipment arrives.
case1.setup: Zahw Store · Wireless headphones · On the way
case1.contact.wathba.name: Wathba Delivery
case1.msg.rafeef1: Rafeef Express: your shipment is on hold due to an unpaid delivery fee (18 SAR). To avoid return within 24 hours, pay here: https://rafeef-express-pay.example/f/7XQ2
case1.msg.wathba1: Wathba Delivery: we received your shipment from Zahw Store and it is being prepared for delivery.
case1.msg.wathba2: ur shipment will arrive tmrw between 4 and 8 pm , no fees . contact us thru the app if any change
case1.msg.mama1: Don't be late today, we have guests 😊
case1.order1.title: Wireless headphones
case1.order0.title: Phone case
case1.E1.title: Ordinary mobile number
case1.E1.body: The message came from an ordinary mobile number (05 0000 0011), not the company's sender ID.
case1.E2.title: Different domain
case1.E2.body: The domain is rafeef-express-pay.example; the official one is rafeef-express.example.
case1.E3.title: There is a real order
case1.E3.body: I do have a headphones order from Zahw Store, and it is on the way.
case1.E4.title: Different delivery company
case1.E4.body: The carrier on my order is Wathba Delivery, not Rafeef.
case1.E5.title: Company policy
case1.E5.body: Rafeef's official site: “We never ask for payment by text message. Fees are paid inside the app only.”
case1.E6.title: The company doesn't know my shipment
case1.E6.body: Rafeef's agent on the official number: “There is no shipment under your name.”
case1.E7.title: A page asking for a card and a code
case1.E7.body: The page imitates the company and asks for full card details and a verification code, with no order number.
case1.E8.title: My real carrier: no fees
case1.E8.body: A genuine, sloppily written notice from Wathba Delivery: the shipment arrives tomorrow and there are no fees.
case1.D1: I really do have a shipment, but with a different company. Having an order wasn't enough proof.
case1.D2: The link isn't the company's site, and its policy never sends payment links in the first place.
case1.D3: The company named in the message doesn't know my shipment.
case1.D4: My real carrier says: no fees. The polished message is the fake one.
case1.dec.pay: Pay the fee through the link
case1.dec.callMsgNumber: Call the number in the message
case1.dec.ignore: Ignore the message and delete it
case1.dec.officialAppReport: Open the official Wathba app to check your shipment, then report the message
case1.out.pay: Your card details were taken. Two days later a 2,300 SAR withdrawal appeared, and you had to freeze the card and go through the bank.
case1.out.callMsgNumber: A friendly “agent” answered and asked for the verification code “to confirm identity”. No real company asks for the code.
case1.out.ignore: You're safe. But the same message keeps targeting others, and no report stops it.
case1.out.officialAppReport: The official app says: delivery tomorrow, no fees. Your report helped block the number.
case1.alt.pay: If you had paid: 18 SAR today, 2,300 SAR in two days, and a frozen card.
case1.alt.callMsgNumber: If you had called the number: pressure to share the code, and the code is the key.
case1.alt.ignore: If you had ignored it: safety for you, zero protection for others.
case1.alt.officialAppReport: If you had checked the app and reported: your shipment is fine and the number is blocked.
case1.plan: The scammer bets that you really are expecting a parcel. A polished message in the name of a known delivery company, a small amount, a short deadline, and a lookalike link. The goal isn't 18 SAR; it's your card details and verification code.
case1.family.q1: Are you actually expecting a parcel, and with which company?
case1.family.q2: Does the company ask for payment by message, or inside its app?
case1.family.q3: Did you check the official app before paying?

case2.title: Someone You Know
case2.intro: Your cousin Reema has been saved in your phone for years. Today two messages arrive from a new number with her photo.
case2.contact.reema.name: Cousin Reema
case2.msg.new1: Hey ❤️ this is my new number, my phone fell and broke this morning. Save it.
case2.msg.new2: Can I ask a favor? I have a transfer due today and my app isn't working on the new number. Send me 850 SAR and I'll return it tomorrow. Don't tell anyone, Mom will be upset.
case2.msg.reema1: Dodo where's the summary you said you'd send 😤
case2.msg.reema4: Mom says come over tomorrow afternoon
case2.msg.reema5: wheeere r u ? been texting since morning
case2.msg.bank1: Ofuq Bank: a transfer of 150 SAR was made from your account. Never share your verification code.
case2.msg.bank2: Ofuq Bank: purchase of 32 SAR at Al-Murjan Restaurant. If this wasn't you, call the official number printed on your card.
case2.reply.cat: Ok but first: what's Grandma's cat called? 😄
case2.reply.cat.response: lol what's the cat got to do with it? Please just send it, it's urgent, we'll chat later
case2.reply.call: Why don't you just call? Easier
case2.reply.call.response: Calls don't work on the new number, only messages. Send it and I'll call tomorrow
case2.reply.later: Let me check and get back to you
case2.reply.later.response: No, now!! If you're late the service gets cut off. Please
case2.E1.title: Photo matches
case2.E1.body: The new number's photo is identical to Reema's saved photo.
case2.E2.title: Different style
case2.E2.body: Reema calls me “Dodo” and sends voice notes. The new number did neither.
case2.E3.title: A message from the old number after the “break”
case2.E3.body: Two hours ago Reema texted me from her old number (“wheeere r u”), after the morning the new number says her phone broke.
case2.E4.title: A money request with every trick
case2.E4.body: Money + urgency (today) + secrecy (don't tell anyone) + a new number, all in one message.
case2.E5.title: Reema didn't change her number
case2.E5.body: I called the saved old number: Reema says “I never changed my number, what are you talking about?!”
case2.E6.title: Dodges the personal question
case2.E6.body: I asked for Grandma's cat's name; the sender dodged and pushed for the transfer again.
case2.D1: Reema texted me from her old number after her phone “broke”, in her usual style. A contradiction in time and style.
case2.D2: The photo really matches, but Reema herself on the old number confirms she never changed it. A photo proves nothing.
case2.D3: The request carries every scam trick, and the sender dodges the simplest personal question.
case2.dec.transfer: Send the money; Reema only asks when she needs it
case2.dec.askPersonal: Ask a personal question in the same chat first
case2.dec.callOldTellFamily: Call Reema's old number and tell her family
case2.dec.blockOnly: Block the number and do nothing else
case2.out.transfer: You lost 850 SAR. An hour later a second message asked for 1,200 “for an emergency”. The number vanished the next day.
case2.out.askPersonal: The dodge exposed them, but you stayed in the channel they chose, and nobody in the family was warned.
case2.out.callOldTellFamily: Reema on her old number was shocked, the whole family knew within minutes, and the number was blocked before it reached your grandmother.
case2.out.blockOnly: You're safe, but the same message reached your aunt that evening and nobody had warned her.
case2.alt.transfer: If you had sent it: 850 SAR today, a second request tomorrow, then the number disappears.
case2.alt.askPersonal: If you had asked in the same chat: exposed, but still in their channel.
case2.alt.callOldTellFamily: If you had called the old number: the truth in seconds, and the family protected.
case2.alt.blockOnly: If you had only blocked: you're fine, and the scammer moves on to the next person.
case2.plan: The scammer doesn't need to know Reema. Her public photo and the words “your cousin” are enough. A touching story (a broken phone), a reasonable amount, an excuse not to call, and a secret that stops you asking anyone. The goal is to keep you in the channel they chose.
case2.family.q1: Did you verify the person through their old number or face to face?
case2.family.q2: Why the secrecy? An honest request isn't afraid of family.
case2.family.q3: Do a photo or a name alone prove identity? (No.)
case2.call.reema.l1: Hey Dodo! Where have you been all morning?
case2.call.reema.l2: Reema… did you change your number? A new number with your photo is asking me for 850 SAR.
case2.call.reema.l3: I never changed my number, what are you talking about?! My phone is in my hand right now!
case2.call.reema.l4: So someone's impersonating you. I'm telling Auntie now.
case2.call.reema.l5: Don't send anything! I'll warn everyone.
case3.title: The Fake Prize
case3.intro: Two months ago you entered Lamha Store's “Winter Draw” and didn't win. Today a private message arrives from an account called Lamha.Rewards.
case3.setup: Lamha Store · old entry in the Winter Draw
case3.contact.rewards.name: Lamha.Rewards
case3.order1.title: Phone case
case3.msg.rew1: Congratulations! You've been selected as a winner in the “Lamha Spring” draw: a 50,000 SAR prize. To claim it, pay the 350 SAR verification fee before midnight: https://lamha-rewards-claim.example
case3.msg.bank1: Ofuq Bank: a salary of 3,000 SAR was deposited into your account.
case3.msg.bankOtp: Ofuq Bank: verification code 4821 for a transaction of 2,950 SAR at an online merchant. Never share the code with anyone.
case3.E1.title: A 4-day-old account
case3.E1.body: The account is unverified, 4 days old, with only 9 posts. A real store has years of history and followers.
case3.E2.title: Different domain
case3.E2.body: The domain is lamha-rewards-claim.example; the official one is lamha-store.example.
case3.E3.title: Contest policy
case3.E3.body: Lamha's official site: “Winners are announced from our official account only and we never ask for fees.” The latest draw is the “Winter Draw”.
case3.E4.title: I never entered “Lamha Spring”
case3.E4.body: My record shows only an old entry in the “Winter Draw”. There is no “Lamha Spring” draw I took part in.
case3.E5.title: The store denies the draw
case3.E5.body: Lamha support on the official number: “There is no draw by that name, and we never charge winners fees.”
case3.E6.title: A code for 2,950, not 350
case3.E6.body: As soon as the link opened, a bank code arrived for a 2,950 SAR transaction, not the 350 the page shows.
case3.D1: I never entered this draw in the first place, and the store doesn't announce winners by private message.
case3.D2: The store itself denies the draw exists and confirms there are no fees.
case3.D3: The code is for 2,950 SAR, not 350, and the link isn't the store's site. The page charges a different amount from what it shows.
case3.dec.shareOtp: Share the verification code “to confirm receipt”
case3.dec.payFee: Pay the 350 fee through the link
case3.dec.refuseFreezeReport: Refuse the code, freeze the card from the official bank app, and report the account
case3.out.shareOtp: 2,950 SAR were withdrawn within seconds. The code was the last key, and the bank treats the transaction as authorized because you shared it.
case3.out.payFee: You lost 350 SAR and the scammer now has your card details. Two days later, purchase attempts from abroad appeared.
case3.out.ignore: You're safe, but the fake account keeps messaging others, and nobody reported it.
case3.out.refuseFreezeReport: Card frozen from the official app, the fake account reported and closed within a day, and you didn't lose a riyal.
case3.alt.shareOtp: If you had shared the code: 2,950 SAR gone instantly.
case3.alt.payFee: If you had paid: 350 today, and an exposed card for weeks.
case3.alt.ignore: If you had ignored it: safety for you, zero protection for others.
case3.alt.refuseFreezeReport: If you had refused, frozen and reported: zero loss, and a scam account shut down.
case3.plan: The scammer starts with a big prize and a small fee so the request looks reasonable. They use a store you know and a contest that resembles one you really entered. The fake page doesn't want the 350 SAR; it wants your card details and the verification code for a much larger transaction.
case3.family.q1: Did you actually enter this contest, under this name?
case3.family.q2: Why would a winner pay? A real prize has no fees.
case3.family.q3: Does the amount in the verification code match what you think you're paying? Never share the code.

consent.title: Before we start
consent.what.title: What is this game?
consent.what.body: An educational game that trains you to spot scam messages by investigating. About 20 minutes: 6 messages, 3 cases, 6 messages, then 8 feedback questions.
consent.data.title: What data is saved?
consent.data.body: Only your in-game answers with an anonymous tester code. No name, number or email, and no server or tracking. Everything stays on your device until you copy the results code and send it yourself.
consent.ask.title: What do we ask of you?
consent.ask.body: Play calmly without help and answer honestly. There is no wrong answer in the feedback questions.
consent.rights.title: Your rights
consent.rights.body: Taking part is voluntary and you can stop at any time. All names and companies are fictional and no real link is ever opened.
consent.agree: I have read the above and agree to take part
consent.guardian: I am under 16 and my guardian agrees to my taking part
consent.note: Requiring guardian consent under 16 is the project team's own policy.
debrief.misleading.why: It looks like it supports the message, but it is not enough on its own.
debrief.distractor.title: The interrupting message was not evidence
debrief.distractor.body: The bank alert that arrived mid-investigation is genuine, but it has nothing to do with this case. Not every message that arrives while you investigate is a clue.

family.title: Family card: before you believe it
family.subtitle: Three questions and one habit that protect your mother, your grandmother and anyone you love from scam messages.
family.general.title: Ask yourself first
family.general.q1: Am I actually expecting this message? (a parcel, a transfer, an appointment)
family.general.q2: Does it ask for money, a code or details, and rush me or ask for secrecy?
family.general.q3: Can I check without using the link or number that came in the message?
family.habit.title: The habit: the other channel
family.habit.body: Never verify through the channel the message came from. Open the official app yourself, call a saved number or the one printed on your card, or type the website address yourself.
family.footer: Educational game: every name and number is fictional. Real or Ruse? is built by Deema Majid AlMaarik.
